Bitcoin (BTC/USD) — Weekly Outlook



Bitcoin has sold off sharply over the past two weeks as fear swept back through the crypto market. The main catalyst was Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) confirming its first Bitcoin sale since 2022 — small in dollar terms, but enough to break the long-standing "Saylor never sells" narrative and shake sentiment, with broader market pressure compounding the move.
From a technical standpoint, price is now testing a major support confluence on the weekly chart. Three independent levels meet right here: the 200-week moving average, which has repeatedly acted as a launchpad for BTC in previous cycles; the long-term ascending trendline; and the 0.382 Fibonacci retracement at $58,401. When this many supports stack into a single zone, it carries far more weight than any one level on its own.

That said, we are not calling a bottom yet. As marked on the chart, we want to see a clean breakout above the falling wedge, confirmed by a pickup in volume, before considering an entry. Until that confirmation arrives, we remain risk-off and recommend no action for now.

Bitcoin (BTC) dominance is experiencing a significant upward trend, posting a notable 0.6% gain today alone. Currently hovering around 60.90%, dominance has reached a level that traditionally signals high risk for altcoins, which explains Bitcoin's recent outperformance against the broader crypto market.

Historically, this capital rotation is a classic hallmark of early bull market cycles. Large-volume players typically liquidate altcoin positions into Bitcoin to fuel its initial ascent. Once Bitcoin eventually establishes a new range and consolidates—leading to a drop in BTC dominance—capital typically flows back into the broader market, triggering a strong altcoin rally.

Until that rotation occurs, we recommend remaining highly selective with altcoin exposure.
